WHAT_WAS_BUILT.consumer: consumeSettlementClaims() — turns ArbitrationRequest objects from CHALLENGE_FACT_VALIDITY into reviewable SettlementClaim records and changes no status; ledgerUnchanged is typed as the literal true

AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY.howItIsStructural: the authority carries a REAL module-private symbol brand, not a type-only one, so an object satisfying the interface cannot be constructed outside the module — a forged authority is an impossible value rather than a silenceable type error
AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY.scope: SINGLE_FACT_SINGLE_CLAIM_SINGLE_USE, with impliesFutureSufficiency typed as the literal false so an approval says this evidence settled this fact this once and nothing about the next identical-looking evidence

REVIEW_CONTRACT.whyTheRefusedListIsEnumerated: HISTORICAL_EVALUATION_LABEL is the §162/§169 disposition that must never re-enter the loop it judges; AUTOMATED_MATCHER is the scorer §160/§161 retired. Naming them makes an accidental promotion a refusal with a code rather than an omission nobody notices.
REVIEW_CONTRACT.whyNoDegree: a reviewer who is unsure returns LEAVE_UNRESOLVED, which produces the same outcome as doing nothing — and which is the right answer whenever the governed criterion cannot settle the property, a situation §181 showed will be common

REPLAY_AND_STALENESS.claimId: sha256 over (contract version, analysisId, factKey, providerReason) — the same claim always yields the same id; a different reason yields a different one
REPLAY_AND_STALENESS.evidenceDigest: sha256 over the reason text alone, so an approval cannot be replayed against edited evidence
REPLAY_AND_STALENESS.whyThisAndNoMore: §182 asked for the smallest development-scoped form necessary. No revision subsystem was invented: application compares the fact's current status against factStatusAtClaim (LEDGER_MOVED_SINCE_CLAIM), and the pre-existing transition() independently throws on a terminal status.
REPLAY_AND_STALENESS.duplicateProtection: appliedClaimIds is carried BY THE CALLER rather than in module state, so replay protection is explicit at the call site instead of hidden global memory

CLAIM_BOUNDARY.permittedAndProven: The existing inactive settlement architecture now contains a human-authorized path capable of transitioning a bound owed fact to SETTLED_BY_EVIDENCE, while provider claims alone cannot do so.
CLAIM_BOUNDARY.why: no model ran and no behaviour was measured. This is implementation evidence about what the architecture can and cannot do, not about what a provider or a reviewer will do with it.
